_comment: ACK LEDGER for scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh _check_launchd_agents (FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-ACKED-LAUNCHD-DEATH-SUPPRESSION, 2026-07-23). A listed `label` whose launchd check currently fails (not-loaded OR non-zero exit status) is reported as acknowledged-degraded instead of a fresh failure: if every unhealthy launchd label found this run is in this list, the probe still returns ALL_GREEN (with the acknowledged labels named in `detail` for transparency) so the Tier-1 cron does not re-spawn system-auditor every ~30min tick re-confirming a signature that already has an open backlog fix-task. A NEW/unacknowledged failure (label absent from this list) always still fails the check, even alongside acked ones — acknowledgment never masks a fresh signature. STALENESS RULE: remove an entry once its `tracked_by` task reaches DONE_VERIFIED — a stale entry left here after the underlying fix ships would silently re-suppress a REAL regression forever. THE STALENESS RULE IS NOW CODE-ENFORCED, not prose-only (FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY, 2026-07-29): `_launchd_label_acked()` resolves `tracked_by` against every docs/data/orch/orch-state.json task_board lane on every probe run — an entry whose `tracked_by` is absent from every lane, OR has reached DONE_VERIFIED, no longer suppresses; the probe reports it as a fresh STALE-ACK failure instead. You may still remove a stale entry by hand for tidiness, but leaving one here past its tracked task's DONE_VERIFIED no longer silently re-suppresses anything. Read-only from the probe's point of view; edited by hand (PO/developer) when a launchd death gets triaged into a tracked backlog row, or when that row closes.

_comment_acked_memory: ACK LEDGER for the SAME probe's _check_mem_creep (FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-A30-MEM-SINGLE-CONTAINER-SCOPE, 2026-07-25). A listed `container` value is matched (case-insensitive substring) against the full name of any RUNNING, memory-capped container whose docker-stats MemPerc breaches WARN_PCT=85: if every breaching container this run is covered, the probe still returns ALL_GREEN (acked containers named in `detail` for transparency). A breach NOT covered here always still fails the check, even alongside acked ones — same mixed-case-never-suppresses guarantee as `acked` above. STALENESS RULE identical: remove the entry once its `tracked_by` task reaches DONE_VERIFIED. Seeded 2026-07-25 with rag-service, whose high steady-state (~94-98% of its 768m cap, healthy/serving throughout) is a detector-scope question, not a detector defect. CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (PO): the seed originally named RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND as the root cause of that steady-state. That was WRONG and is refuted by measurement — see the entry retarget_reason below. The driver is the embedder model singleton (fixed ~700 MiB baseline reached on the first embed), whose ceiling trade is owned by FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY, with the compaction failure-path counter defect owned by FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP. THE STALENESS RULE AND THE ABSOLUTE-HEADROOM GAP ARE NOW BOTH CODE-ENFORCED (FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY, 2026-07-29, supersedes the 'tracked_by is never read' / 'unbounded in both directions' language that was accurate before this fix): `_mem_container_acked()` now (a) resolves `tracked_by` against every orch-state.json task_board lane every run — absent-from-every-lane or DONE_VERIFIED means the entry is a STALE ACK and stops suppressing; (b) computes absolute headroom (cap - usage) and refuses to suppress once it drops below MEM_FLOOR_MIB=40 (calibrated against rag-service's own ~20 MiB measured compact()-failure burst, see FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP, not the cap). See `floor_enforcement_20260729` on the rag-service entry below for the live consequence this has on THIS specific entry. Do NOT resolve staleness via a per-container threshold override (PO DECISION, task FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-A30-MEM-SINGLE-CONTAINER-SCOPE: static overrides are the same lagging-whitelist failure mode as FIX-AUDITOR-D4-WHITELIST-DATA-QUALITY-ANOMALY-PREFIX and would also silently swallow a REAL rag OOM approach) — MEM_FLOOR_MIB is a single global constant, deliberately not per-container.

acked_memory.retarget_reason: SCOPE MISMATCH + UNREACHABLE SELF-EXPIRY. (1) The prior tracked_by, RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND, bounds _build_fts_index(). It is NOT the driver of the suppressed condition: rag-service reaches ~97% of its 768 MiB cap after a SINGLE embed, with zero FTS activity, because apps/rag-service/infrastructure/embedder.py holds the sentence-transformers model as a lazy singleton with no release path (MEASURED by PO 2026-07-29T10:20-10:28Z: cold RSS 50.7 MiB -> 749.9 MiB after one POST /index; re-measured 756.8 MiB at 11:47Z, i.e. a FIXED anonymous baseline that does not scale with request volume — see memory_split_20260729 below for the cgroup split that establishes this, and note the earlier wording here said 745.8 MiB / flat, which was a stale two-sample reading corrected the same tick). Shipping the FTS row would not lower the number. That row own 2026-07-15 qa_result.idle_baseline_flag already said so verbatim: idle mem ~92% of the 768m bound with ZERO FTS activity — ten days before this ledger was seeded against it. (2) The STALENESS RULE is this ledger only safety promise, and binding it to RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND made it unreachable: that row is blocked_on rag-corpus-repopulation-to-representative-scale, PO-projected testable on/after ~2026-08-16, po_timegate_next_recheck_after 2026-08-12. The ACK could not expire for >=18 days by construction. FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY owns the resident-set / 768m-cap trade, so its DONE_VERIFIED is the event that would genuinely mean rag-service no longer sits at 97% of its cap. ENTRY DELIBERATELY NOT REMOVED: removal flips Tier-1 to FAILURE every ~30min tick and re-spawns system-auditor ~48x/day to re-confirm a known condition — the exact churn FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-ACKED-LAUNCHD-DEATH-SUPPRESSION was minted to kill. READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE FIELD: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh:275 reads ONLY .acked_memory[].container. tracked_by is read by nothing, so this retarget changes NO probe behaviour and the STALENESS RULE remains enforced by prose alone. Making tracked_by load-bearing, plus an absolute-headroom floor the ACK may not swallow, is FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY (backlog, P1).
acked_memory.memory_split_20260729: CGROUP anon/file SPLIT — this is the measurement that decides whether the suppressed condition is dangerous, so it lives here rather than only on the task rows. At the 10:12Z restart the cgroup read anon = 761716736 B (726.4 MiB) immediately pre-restart against ~767 MiB total usage, falling to anon = 32272384 B (30.8 MiB) immediately post-restart. ANON IS ~95% OF THE CGROUP; FILE-BACKED IS AT MOST ~40 MiB. CONSEQUENCE FOR ANYONE REVIEWING THIS SUPPRESSION: the memory is process-resident, NOT reclaimable page cache. There is no kernel reclaim that will rescue this container under pressure, and the ~11 MiB of headroom recorded above is genuinely all there is against a compaction burst documented at ~20 MiB. An earlier reading on the task rows argued the opposite (that a 786 MiB on-disk LanceDB corpus was filling the cgroup as file cache) — that is RETRACTED; 786 MiB on disk versus a 768 MiB cap is a numeric coincidence, not a mechanism, and the corpus is not resident here. PROVENANCE: the two anon figures are router-supplied and were NOT independently re-derived by PO — re-deriving requires reading the VM cgroup tree, and the only route available is a docker exec, which is what allocated inside this cgroup and SIGKILLed the container at 10:12Z (exec exit 137, RestartCount 21->22). DO NOT RE-RUN IT TO CONFIRM. It is independently corroborated in mechanism by a measurement already on FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP: cold RSS 50.7 MiB rising to 749.9 MiB after a SINGLE POST /index, with the model load logged 10:24:28.5Z-10:24:48.9Z — a 699 MiB step from one embed can only be anonymous heap.
acked_memory.suppression_still_warranted: YES as of 2026-07-29T11:50Z, and the reasoning is unchanged by the correction above: the condition is a known, tracked, steady-state consequence of a no-release-path model singleton, and removing this entry would flip Tier-1 to FAILURE every ~30min tick and re-spawn system-auditor ~48x/day to re-confirm it. BUT THE MARGIN IS THINNER THAN THIS LEDGER PREVIOUSLY IMPLIED and the suppression is currently unbounded in both directions: there is no absolute-headroom floor below which the ACK stops suppressing, and tracked_by is read by no code so the entry cannot self-expire. Both are tracked by FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY (backlog, P1). RE-REVIEW THIS ENTRY, do not assume it: if headroom falls below ~5 MiB, or RestartCount/day climbs above ~5 (it is 22 total over 13.8 days = 1.6/day, unmoved since 10:12:01Z), the suppression is no longer appropriate and the entry should be pulled even though its tracked_by row is still open.
acked_memory.floor_enforcement_20260729: FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY LANDED — both gaps `suppression_still_warranted` above flagged as unbounded are now code-enforced (MEM_FLOOR_MIB=40, tracked_by resolved against orch-state.json). LIVE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS EXACT ENTRY: `headroom_mib_at_ack_review` above is 11.2 MiB, well below the 40 MiB floor, while `tracked_by`=FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY currently resolves to a live (BACKLOG, non-DONE_VERIFIED) status — so the entry fails on the BELOW-FLOOR predicate specifically, not staleness. As of this fix landing, the NEXT Tier-1 tick that samples rag-service at or near this headroom will report verdict FAILURE (detail names rag-service, its %, its MiB-free, and BELOW-FLOOR), not ALL_GREEN. THIS IS THE INTENDED, DESIGNED OUTCOME of the fix (its AC2), not a regression: the whole point of this row was that the old all-or-nothing pct>=85 predicate could not distinguish this entry's acknowledged 94-98% steady-state from the genuinely dangerous approach to 0 MiB free that is now measured live. Do not silently raise MEM_FLOOR_MIB or re-widen this ACK to make the FAILURE go away — that would recreate exactly the blind suppression this row exists to close; if the resulting cron churn needs managing, route it to PO for a capacity/cap decision (FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY), not a detector change.
